title: How to Compare Hardwood Refinishing Quotes in Kirkland: What a Real Quote Must Include
meta: Compare Kirkland hardwood refinishing quotes on measured sq ft, scope, coats, stairs, dust and warranty. Wills Flooring lists what a real quote must include.
keywords: compare hardwood floor refinishing quotes, what should a floor refinishing quote include, hardwood refinishing estimate Kirkland, refinishing quote per square foot, floor refinishing bids

blocks.lead: A real refinishing quote states the measured square footage, whether it is a recoat, a natural sand or a stain, the finish product and number of coats, the stair count at a per-tread price, dust containment, repairs, timeline and warranty. If any of those is missing, you cannot compare it.
blocks.detail: Wills Flooring publishes its rates: $3.99 per sq ft natural, $6.50 with stain, $1.99 screen-and-recoat, $55 to $75 per stair, 500 sq ft minimum. Every Kirkland quote we write shows those lines against your measured floor, so you can hold it next to any other bid.

blocks.html: Kirkland homeowners get more refinishing bids than most, partly because Eastside remodel budgets are bigger and partly because the resale bar in Houghton, Juanita and Bridle Trails is high enough that a mediocre floor costs money later. The problem is that three quotes for the same Rose Hill split-level rarely describe the same job. One is a lump sum. One is per square foot but counts the whole house. One is cheap because it quietly drops a coat of finish. Here is how to read them so the lowest number is also the best value.

blocks.text: The eight things a real quote must show

items.html: Measured square footage of the floor being refinished. Not the house size from the listing, not "about 1,000". Closets in or out should be stated.
The scope in plain words. Screen and recoat, sand and finish natural, or sand, stain and finish. These are three different jobs at three different prices.
The finish product, sheen and number of coats. Three coats of a named water-based finish is the standard we work to. Two coats of an unnamed product is a different floor.
Stairs counted and priced per tread. A staircase folded into the square footage is either underpriced or hidden.
Dust containment, and what it means. Vacuum-connected sanders are standard for us. Sealing and an air scrubber is a $250 line, not a vague promise of dustless.
Repairs and board replacement. Either priced per board or clearly marked as quoted on site after inspection.
Days on site and when you can walk on it. A quote with no schedule usually becomes a longer job than promised.
Warranty, license and insurance in writing. Ours is a 1-year workmanship warranty, and we are Bona Certified Craftsmen, which you can verify.

blocks.text: Where a low quote hides its cost

items.title: The third coat
items.text: Finish is the wear surface. Two coats look the same on day one and show traffic lanes in two years. On a Kirkland floor that has to impress a buyer in five years, the third coat is the cheapest insurance on the quote.

items.title: Edges, closets and under toe-kicks
items.text: The big machine does the middle of the room fast. Edging along walls, inside closets and under kitchen toe-kicks is slow hand work, and it is what a rushed crew skips. Ask whether closets are in the square footage.

items.title: The staircase
items.text: A Juanita two-story with 14 stairs is $770 to $1,050 of tread work at our rates. A quote that does not mention stairs either forgot them or plans to add them on the last day.

items.title: Dry time
items.text: Water-based finish needs real hours between coats. A crew promising a stained floor in two days is either skipping coats or rushing them, and rushed coats peel.

blocks.text: Mistakes Kirkland homeowners make when comparing bids

items.html: Comparing a recoat quote to a sanding quote. A $1.99 screen-and-recoat is a great deal if your finish is intact and worthless if it is worn through. Make sure every bidder agrees on which job your floor needs. Our post on refinish or recoat shows how to tell.
Picking the lowest per-foot rate without the coat count. Per foot means nothing until you know what is in the foot.
Letting each company measure differently. One counts closets, one does not, one counts the whole footprint. Walk each estimator through the same rooms and ask for the number.
Ignoring the schedule. A cheaper crew that takes seven days in an occupied Houghton house costs you a week of hotel or chaos.
Not asking who is actually doing the work. Some bids come from a salesperson and the job goes to a subcontractor you never met. Ask, and ask for the warranty in the company's name.

blocks.text: Questions to ask every bidder before you decide

items: What square footage did you measure, and does it include closets?
Is this a recoat, a natural sand or a stain job, and why did you recommend that?
Which finish, which sheen, and how many coats?
How are stairs priced, and how many did you count?
What is included for dust control, and what does it cost?
How many days on site, and when can we walk on it and move furniture back?
Is the workmanship warranty written into the quote, and are you licensed and insured?

faq.q: What is a fair price per square foot to refinish hardwood floors in Kirkland?
faq.a: Wills Flooring's published rates are $3.99 per sq ft for a natural sand and finish, $6.50 with stain and $1.99 for a screen-and-recoat, with a 500 sq ft minimum. Stairs are $55 to $75 per tread. Compare other quotes against those numbers only after confirming the same scope and coat count.

faq.q: Why do refinishing quotes vary so much for the same house?
faq.a: Usually because they describe different jobs. One includes stairs and three coats of finish, another two coats and no stairs, a third bills the whole house footprint instead of the hardwood. Line up square footage, scope, coats and extras before you compare totals.

faq.q: Should I choose the cheapest hardwood refinishing quote?
faq.a: Only if it matches the others on scope. The cheapest way to lower a quote is to drop a coat of finish or skip edge work, and those savings show up as worn traffic lanes within a couple of years. On a Kirkland home with high resale expectations that is a poor trade.

faq.q: How many coats of finish should a refinishing quote include?
faq.a: Three. Two coats look fine on day one but wear faster, and the third coat is what protects the wood in hallways and kitchens. Our standard is three coats of Bona water-based finish, and the quote names the product and sheen.

faq.q: Does a refinishing quote include moving furniture?
faq.a: It should say either way. We handle it case by case: most Kirkland customers clear rooms themselves, and large pieces can be moved for a flat fee stated on the quote. Washer and dryer moves are $160 per pair and other appliances $80 each at our published rates.

faq.q: How long should a refinishing quote be valid?
faq.a: Ask. Most written quotes hold for 30 days. Ours is a firm written price handed to you at the estimate, based on what we measured, and it does not change unless we find damage that was hidden under carpet or furniture at the visit.
